S01.name: ZEBRA Na|beta''-Al2O3|NaAlCl4|NiCl2 (tubular, 270-350 C)
S01.flammable: No organic solvent; molten Na is reactive (contained by ceramic + steel)
S01.tox_note: Ni (sensitiser, Carc. 2 for powder), AlCl3/NaAlCl4 releases HCl with water
S01.manuf_note: beta''-alumina ceramic + glass/TCB seals; few qualified suppliers
S01.recyc_note: Ni/steel recovered in stainless-steel melt (historical practice)
S01.salt_link: NaCl is the discharged cathode feed (cell assembled from NaCl + Ni powder); Na metal forms in situ on first charge
S01.cathode: Ni/NaCl granules (+FeS, NaF, Al additives) in NaAlCl4 melt
S01.E_source: OCV 2.58 V at 300 C [PUBLISHED, PS-008/PS-010]; 2.64 V from 298 K thermochemistry [CALCULATED, S11]

S02.name: IT planar Na|beta''-Al2O3|NaAlCl4|NiCl2 (190 C)
S02.manuf_note: Planar ceramic discs + seals at lower T; pilot only
S02.salt_link: Same as S01; planar format at 190 C (PNNL)

S03.name: IT planar Na|beta''-Al2O3|NaAlCl4|FeCl2 (Fe + 10% Ni, 190 C)
S03.tox_note: Fe benign; AlCl3 hydrolysis to HCl remains
S03.salt_link: Assembled discharged from NaCl + Fe powder (+S additive) - salt and iron only for the active couple
S03.E_source: OCV 2.35 V (Fe/FeCl2 vs Na, ~300 C) [PUBLISHED]; 2.41 V 298 K thermochemistry [CALCULATED, S11]

S04.name: RT Na|AlCl3-SOCl2|Cl2-in-carbon (Na-Cl2)
S04.flammable: Non-flammable solvent but SOCl2 is acutely toxic/corrosive; Cl2 gas on overcharge/abuse
S04.tox_note: SOCl2 (fatal if inhaled, reacts with water -> SO2 + HCl); Cl2 gas
S04.manuf_note: Li/SOCl2 primary-cell lines exist; rechargeable never manufactured
S04.salt_link: NaCl <-> Na + 1/2 Cl2 is the reaction itself; Cl2 stored in microporous carbon
S04.rxn_cathode: 1/2 Cl2 + Na+ + e- -> NaCl (in carbon pores)
S04.E_source: dG_f(NaCl) = -384.1 kJ/mol -> 3.98 V [CALCULATED]; cells run ~3.5 V [PUBLISHED PS-001]

N01.name: Na-ion layered oxide|hard carbon (NaPF6 carbonate)
N01.recyc_note: Hydromet; Al on both sides eases
N01.competitors: CATL Naxtra, BYD, HiNa, Faradion/Reliance, Gotion
N01.salt_link: Na from Na2CO3 (Solvay route from NaCl in India; trona in USA)

N02.name: Na-ion NFPP|hard carbon
N02.competitors: Peak Energy (cells from China), Alsym 'NFPP+', many Chinese makers

N03.name: Na-ion Prussian white|hard carbon
N03.tox_note: Cyanide-bridged lattice (HCN release only in fire/strong acid)
N03.manuf_note: Water removal is the hard step

N04.name: Na-ion NVPF|hard carbon (high power)
N04.salt_link: Na2CO3; vanadium is the critical input

N05.name: Aqueous Na-ion birnessite|NaTi2(PO4)3 (0.5 M Na2SO4) - prior track B
N05.salt_link: Na2SO4 electrolyte; Na from Na2CO3/NaOH (both from NaCl in India)

N06.name: Aqueous Na-ion MnFe-PBA|NaTi2(PO4)3 (perchlorate-free) - prior track C

N07.name: Quasi-solid Na-ion NVP|NASICON|hard carbon
N07.manuf_note: Thin ceramic films are hard to make cheaply

N08.name: Anode-free Na solid-state: layered oxide|sulfide/halide SE|Al CC
N08.flammable: Low; sulfide SE releases H2S with moisture
N08.tox_note: H2S from sulfide SE; Na metal
N08.manuf_note: High stack pressure, thin SE, no mass process
N08.salt_link: Na2CO3 for cathode; Na inventory comes entirely from the cathode
N08.electrolyte: Na3PS4 / Na3SbS4 / NaxMCl6 halide or borohydride

N09.name: RT Na-S: Na|glyme|S/C (Na2S end)
N09.tox_note: Na metal; polysulfides; H2S with acid/moisture
N09.salt_link: Na metal (Downs cell from NaCl) + sulfur (refinery by-product)

N10.name: HT Na-S (NAS): Na|beta''-Al2O3|S (300-350 C)
N10.salt_link: Na metal loaded at assembly (Downs cell, NaCl feed)
N10.E_source: OCV 2.08 V (Na2S5 region) to 1.78 V; avg ~1.95 V [PUBLISHED]

N11.name: Na-O2 (NaO2 superoxide), Na|glyme|carbon air electrode
N11.T_op: RT, dry pure O2 in lab
N11.salt_link: Na metal from NaCl (Downs); O2 from air

N12.name: Organic: Na|carbonate|Na2C6O6 (rhodizonate) or quinone
N12.salt_link: Na from NaOH/Na2CO3; organic carbonyl cathode

N13.name: Na|FeS2 conversion (pyrite), carbonate/glyme
N13.salt_link: Na metal or pre-sodiated Na2S/Fe; pyrite is mined

A01.name: Aqueous Zn-ion: Zn|ZnSO4|MnO2
A01.competitors: Eos (Zn hybrid), Enerpoly, Salient, Alsym (Zn-MnO2 per press)

A04.name: Al-ion: Al|AlCl3-EMIm-Cl|graphite
A04.salt_link: AlCl3 made by chlorinating Al (Cl from chlor-alkali / NaCl)
A04.E_source: avg ~1.8-2.0 V; electrolyte is a reactant [PUBLISHED]
